newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia propels Finnish shares to record high close.
newsitem.headline: Nokia propels Finnish shares to record high close.

text.p: A rally in Nokia on Friday propelled the HEX index to a new all-time high close of 2,367.50 on Friday, up 5.5 percent for the week.
It was the second day of frenzied trading in Nokia, which rose sharply on demand sparked by the telecom group's third quarter earnings report on Thursday.
Volume was unusually heavy for Helsinki at 1.1 billion markka, with 68 percent of total bourse turnover in Nokia.
Brokers saw scope for further gains next week as the tone was strong after two consecutive record sessions.
"Nokia is likely to remain in focus next week. I think it will take the whole stock market higher," one broker said.
Nokia closed massive trade 7.00 markka higher at 259.00 -- its highest close since October 19, 1995 -- after touching 267.50 markka during the session.
Gains in Nokia fuelled forestries and particularly UPM-Kymmene, which holds nine percent of votes in Nokia.
Reports of a smaller than expected rise in North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) pulp inventories in October also helped paper stocks, brokers said.
Merita bank's most-traded A share closed moderate trade 0.30 markka up at 14.20.
But wholesaler and retailer Kesko fell 1.50 markka to 65.00, hit by news that an EU source said he expected the European Commission to decide against the merger of Kesko with its former rival Tuko.
Prefab log house builder Honkarakenne closed up 2.00 markka at 25.00 after announcing a 40 percent year-on-year rise in orders.
